title: Agroecology for Africa
provider: FAO elearning Academy (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations), with the Alliance for Food Sovereignty in Africa (AFSA) and the McKnight Foundation
language: English and French (verified on course page). No Russian version found.
cost: Free (no fee for enrollment, course materials, exam, or digital badge)
certificate: Digital badge (open-badge style) issued automatically on passing the final certification exam with a grade of at least 75%. Self-paced; no facilitator. Number of exam retake attempts not stated on the page [UNVERIFIED].
duration: Approximately 3 hours 45 minutes total (4 lessons, each ~45-70 minutes). Self-paced, asynchronous.
level: Introductory-to-intermediate (conceptual/policy orientation; not stated explicitly on the page — inferred from content and audience). [UNVERIFIED exact level label]
target_audience: Government officials in ministries of agriculture, food security, environment, health, trade, economics or rural affairs; policymakers and advisors; and training/capacity-development practitioners. Oriented to the African context.

syllabus.topics: Key concepts and definition of agroecology; framing of agroecology as a science, practice and social movement; the 10 Elements of Agroecology framework (recycling, efficiency, diversity, resilience, synergies, co-creation of knowledge, human and social values, culture and food traditions, responsible governance, circular and solidarity economy); contribution to sustainable agrifood-system transformation. ~45-70 min.

syllabus.module: Lesson 2 — Applying the ecological principles of agroecology
syllabus.topics: Ecological/agronomic dimension: recycling, input-use efficiency, biodiversity and diversification, synergies, soil health, and resilience at field and agroecosystem level; how ecological principles improve agroecosystem health and farm resilience. ~45-70 min.

syllabus.module: Lesson 3 — Applying the social principles of agroecology
syllabus.topics: Social and economic dimension: co-creation and sharing of knowledge, human and social values, culture and food traditions, responsible governance, and circular/solidarity economy; equity and inclusion in agrifood systems. ~45-70 min.

syllabus.module: Lesson 4 — Scaling up and scaling out agroecology
syllabus.topics: How governments, civil society and the private sector enable adoption; scaling up (institutions/policy) and scaling out (geographic spread); enabling environments, with African practical examples and case studies. ~45-70 min.

format: Browser-based, self-paced e-learning (SCORM-style interactive modules; requires pop-ups and a modern browser — Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari). Downloadable PDF course summary and an offline-downloadable full course package (~67.8 MB) are provided.
assessment: Single final certification exam at the end of the course; pass threshold 75%. Per-lesson quiz/knowledge-check details are not specified on the public page. [UNVERIFIED per-lesson quizzes]
hands_on: No technical hands-on/lab work; the course is conceptual and policy-oriented. "Practical" content is delivered through real-world African examples and case studies illustrating uptake and scaling, not through software or field exercises. [UNVERIFIED whether any embedded interactive exercises exist beyond case studies]
tools: None required beyond a modern web browser with pop-ups enabled. No GIS, coding, or specialized software. Downloadable PDF summary and full course package for offline use.
strengths: Genuinely free, including the certifying digital badge — matches a $0-cost stack
Clear, compact 4-lesson structure (~3h45) that is easy to complete and re-skin into a module sequence
Built on FAO's authoritative '10 Elements of Agroecology' framework (endorsed by 197 FAO members) — credible, citable conceptual backbone
Bilingual delivery (EN/FR) demonstrates a working multilingual single-course model
Logical pedagogical arc: concept -> ecological principles -> social principles -> scaling, separating ecological from social dimensions
Self-paced, browser-only, with an offline-downloadable package (~68 MB) and PDF summary — good for low-connectivity rural learners
Automatic badge issuance on a defined 75% threshold — simple, transparent certification rule
Heavy use of real regional case studies to ground abstract principles
weaknesses: No Russian (or Central Asian) localization — content and case studies are Africa-specific, not transferable to North Kazakhstan SMB context
Audience is government officials/policymakers, not SMB agro-practitioners — framing is policy/advocacy, not on-farm how-to
No technical hands-on, data, tools, notebooks, or field-method instruction — purely conceptual
Short and high-level; insufficient depth for skill certification of practitioners
Single end-of-course exam with no stated per-lesson formative assessment limits learning reinforcement
Number of exam attempts and detailed grading rules not transparent on the public page
No regional crop/economic specificity (e.g., grain-belt steppe agriculture) — examples won't resonate with СКО/Костанай/Акмола audiences
